segments.he: צָרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר לַחֲטף כָּל מַה שֶּׁיּוּכַל
segments.en: Therefore Tehillim consists of five books corresponding to the five books of the Torah — for King Dovid made from the five books of Torah five books of prayer and supplication. He thus "made prayers from the Torah teachings," which is the ultimate completeness of prayer. And therefore the essential awakening of teshuvah is through Tehillim — for the essential teshuvah is attained by making prayers from the Torah teachings, which is the aspect of Tehillim.

segments.he: עִקַּר הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּאֲמִינִים בְּהַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנַּ"ל שֶׁמְּלא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ וְכוּ'. אֲבָל תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאִין עָלָיו קֻשְׁיוֹת וַאֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁקָּשֶׁה לוֹ עַל עַצְמוֹ עַל שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי כֵן הוּא פָּגוּם כָּל כָּךְ וְרָחוֹק כָּל כָּךְ מִקְּדֻשַּׁת הַתּוֹרָה אֲזַי תֵּכֶף צָרִיךְ לִבְרחַ מִכָּל אֵלּוּ הַקֻּשְׁיוֹת וְלִשְׁתּק בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וּלְקַיֵּם סְיָג לַחָכְמָה שְׁתִיקָה.
segments.en: This is why we blow the shofar and pray the Malkhuyos [Kingship verses] and so on — all within the Musaf [additional] prayer. For Tefillas Musaf is devoted entirely to praying about the sacrifices that we should have offered in the Holy Temple — but due to our many sins the Temple was destroyed, and we cannot offer them. So we pray to Hashem for the rebuilding of the Temple so that we may again offer the sacrifices, as we say: "Due to our sins we were exiled from our land…" and "There we shall offer before You…" Thus Tefillas Musaf is itself the aspect of making a prayer from a Torah teaching — from the mitzvah of the Musaf sacrifice, we make a prayer. Through this we continue the path of making prayers from the Torah teachings. And each person according to how far he has strayed from fulfilling any commandment — whether a positive or negative one — must pray to Hashem to merit its fulfillment. This is exactly the aspect of Tefillas Musaf — praying to merit what we cannot currently fulfill due to our sins in this time of exile. And such prayer is counted in lieu of the sacrifice. And through this we will ultimately return to our land and offer the sacrifices. So too the prayers one makes from Torah teachings — begging Hashem greatly to merit what is currently so difficult for us in our soul's exile — through these prayers we will ultimately return to Hashem. And even as long as we have not yet merited complete redemption of the soul, the prayer itself counts as though we had fulfilled all our obligations. Thus Tefillas Musaf is the aspect of making prayers from the Torah teachings — and for this reason we blow the shofar and pray Malkhuyos, Zikhronos, and Shoforos at that time — all to establish this path of making prayers from the Torah.

segments.he: רַק לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל פַּעַם לַחֲטף אֵיזֶה נְקֻדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת כָּל מַה שֶּׁיּוּכַל תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת וּבִפְרָט תְּפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים וְשִׂיחָה לִפְנֵי קוֹנוֹ וְלִבְלִי לְהִסְתַּכֵּל עַל כָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עָלָיו. כִּי צְרִיכִין לִהְיוֹת עַקְשָׁן גָּדוֹל בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה' כִּי אֵין יוֹדְעִין כְּלָל. רַק לְקַיֵּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁצִּוָּנוּ רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם יֵאוּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם כְּלָל. כִּי לִגְדֻלָּתוֹ אֵין חֵקֶר וְכוּ'. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדִּבַּרְנוּ מִזֶּה כְּבָר בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת. הֲפךְ בָּהֶם וַהֲפךְ בָּהֶם וְכוּ'. כִּי הֵם חַיֶּיךָ לָנֶצַח. (שָׁם אוֹת ס):
segments.en: For example, if someone wants to pray to Hashem to merit fulfilling the mitzvah of tzitzis completely, but does not know the spiritual power of tzitzis — what quality one can break through tzitzis, what level one can attain through it — then one certainly cannot extend the prayer at length enough to break one's heart and arouse Hashem's compassion, for one can only say: "Master of the Universe, grant me to fulfill the mitzvah of tzitzis perfectly." Although this too is very good, one has not yet attained the level of turning one's prayer into compassion and supplication in which one can innovate something. But the essential completeness of prayer in the form of "making prayers from Torah teachings" comes from innovations of Torah wisdom — through which one comes to know the spiritual power of the mitzvos.
